# rustfs_ldap_service_account (Resource)

Create a service account scoped to an LDAP user.

The service account is created via the LDAP-compat admin endpoint
(`PUT /rustfs/admin/v3/idp/ldap/add-service-account`) with the LDAP user's
distinguished name as the target user. The target user must already exist in
the RustFS identity store, which happens when an LDAP identity provider is
configured on the cluster and the user has authenticated. There is no
dedicated LDAP read-back, list or delete endpoint; the resource reads back
through the standard service-account endpoints, and delete removes the account
as a standard service account.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "rustfs_ldap_service_account" "alice_token" {
  access_key = "ldap-sa-alice"
  secret_key = "a-very-secret-key"
  name       = "alice-ci-token"
  user       = "uid=alice,ou=people,dc=example,dc=com"
  policy = jsonencode({
    Version = "2012-10-17"
    Statement = [
      {
        Effect   = "Allow"
        Action   = ["s3:GetObject"]
        Resource = ["arn:aws:s3:::*"]
      }
    ]
  })
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `access_key` (String) Access key of the service account. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `name` (String) Visible name, only for viewing.
- `secret_key` (String, Sensitive) Secret key of the service account.
- `user` (String) LDAP user (distinguished name) the service account is scoped to. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Short description of the scope we plan to use this token.
- `policy` (String) IAM policy document (JSON) the service account is scoped to. Changing this forces a new resource.

## Import

Import is supported using the access key:

```
terraform import rustfs_ldap_service_account.my_sa ldap-sa-alice
```
